facts.statement: Nothosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropterygian reptile that lived during the Triassic period, approximately 245 to 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: Nothosaurus ('false lizard', from the Ancient Greek and ) is an extinct genus of sauropterygian reptile from the Triassic period, approximately 245–228 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Nothosaurus are distributed throughout the former Tethys Ocean, ranging from North Africa and Europe to China.
facts.quote: with fossils being distributed throughout the former Tethys Ocean, from North Africa and Europe to China

facts.statement: Nothosaurus was a semi-oceanic animal with a lifestyle likely similar to that of modern seals.
facts.quote: Nothosaurus was a semi-oceanic animal which most likely had a lifestyle similar to that of today's seals

facts.statement: Nothosaurus was about 4 meters long, possessed long webbed toes, and likely had a fin on its tail.
facts.quote: It was about 4 m, with long, webbed toes and possibly a fin on its tail

facts.statement: Some species of Nothosaurus, such as N. zhangi and N. giganteus, grew larger, reaching up to 5 to 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: However, some species such as N. zhangi and N. giganteus were larger, up to 5 - 7 m

facts.statement: Nothosaurus had a powerful bite capable of holding prey so tightly that few animals could shake free once caught.
facts.quote: Once caught, few animals would be able to shake themselves free from the mouth of Nothosaurus

facts.statement: Trackways reported from Yunnan, China in June 2014 were interpreted as paddle impressions left by Nothosaurus digging into soft seabed to stir up benthic creatures.
facts.quote: Trackways attributed, partly by process of elimination, to a nothosaur that was reported from Yunnan, China in June 2014, were interpreted as the paddle impressions left as the animals dug into soft seabed with rowing motions of their paddles

facts.statement: The type species of Nothosaurus is N. mirabilis, which was named in 1834 from the Germanic Muschelkalk formation.
facts.quote: The type species is N. mirabilis, named in 1834 from the Germanic Muschelkalk

facts.statement: Several Nothosaurus species, including N. marchicus and N. winkelhorsti, have been described from the Lower Muschelkalk in Winterswijk, the Netherlands.
facts.quote: Several species have been described from the Lower Muschelkalk in Winterswijk, the Netherlands, including N. marchicus (and its junior synonym N. winterswijkensis) and N. winkelhorsti

facts.statement: The lost type material of N. schimperi, originally described from Soultz-les-Bains, France, was recently rediscovered and a lectotype was designated.
facts.quote: Recently, the long considered lost type material of N. schimperi Meyer, 1842 from the Lower Muschelkalk of Soultz-les-Bains, Alsace, France, has been rediscovered and a lectotype has been designated

facts.statement: In 2017, the species N. juvenilis, N. youngi, and N. winkelhorsti were formally reclassified and moved to the genus Lariosaurus.
facts.quote: Later, in 2017, the species N. juvenilis, N. youngi, and N. winkelhorsti were formally moved to Lariosaurus

facts.statement: The genus Nothosaurus was originally described by Hunter in 1834.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Hunter, 1834

facts.statement: Nothosaurus has numerous synonyms including Chondriosaurus, Conchiosaurus, Dracontosaurus, Dracosaurus, Elmosaurus, Kolposaurus, Menodon, Oligolycus, Opeosaurus, Paranothosaurus, and Shingyisaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Chondriosaurus Meyer, 1838 Conchiosaurus Meyer, 1834 Conchriosaurus Meyer, 1838 Dracontosaurus Agassiz, 1846 Dracosaururus Romer, 1966 Dracosaurus Agassiz, 1846 Elmosaurus Huene, 1957 Kolposaurus Skuphos, 1893 Menodon Meyer, 1838 Oligolycus Fristch, 1894 Opeosaurus Meyer, 1847 Paranothosaurus Peyer, 1939 Shingyisaurus Young, 1965

facts.statement: Nothosaurus reached a length of about three meters.
facts.quote: Nothosaurus llegaba a medir unos tres metros de longitud

facts.statement: Nothosaurus possessed very sharp, dagger-shaped teeth that interlocked between the upper and lower jaws, creating a perfect trap for fish.
facts.quote: Sus dientes, muy afilados y en forma de dagas, que además encajaban entre sí los de ambas mandíbulas, eran una trampa perfecta para los peces

facts.statement: Nothosaurus could close its mouth with great force, but the muscles required to reopen it were very weak.
facts.quote: Nothosaurus podía cerrar la boca con una gran fuerza pero los músculos que le permitían volver a abrirla eran muy débiles

facts.statement: Well-preserved fossils show that Nothosaurus had webbed feet suitable for both aquatic and terrestrial environments.
facts.quote: Algunos de los fósiles mejor preservados conservan el dibujo de la piel y nos muestran que Nothosaurus tenía pies palmeados, adecuados tanto para el medio acuático como para el terrestre

facts.statement: Due to their characteristics, Nothosaurus specimens likely spent part of their lives on land, moving over sand and rocks.
facts.quote: Por sus características, los ejemplares de Nothosaurus pudieron pasar parte de su vida en tierra firme, sobre la arena y las rocas

facts.statement: Nothosaurus likely came ashore to rest, bask in the sun, catch prey in shoreline pools, and reproduce by laying eggs.
facts.quote: Probablemente arribaban a tierra para tumbarse a descansar y calentarse al sol, capturar presas en los charcos de la orilla y también para procrear poniendo huevos

facts.statement: Nothosaurus was the most common genus in its group, with fossils discovered in widely separated locations including the Netherlands, China, and Spain.
facts.quote: Fue el género más común de su grupo, ya que sus restos se han descubierto en lugares tan distantes entre sí como Países Bajos, China y España

facts.statement: The fossil taxon Nothosaurus was first described in 1834.
facts.quote: Category:Fossil taxa described in 1834

facts.statement: Evidence of vivipary (live birth) was found in seven out of twenty-four studied Nothosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Seven specimens in a studied sample of twenty-four Nothosaurus showed evidence of vivipary

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that vivipary in Nothosaurus may have been an adaptation to increase early survival rates, compensating for high mortality at later life stages.
facts.quote: Vivipary may have been an adaptation for increasing survival early in an individual's life history to compensate for high mortality ates at later life stages

rejected.statement: The Nothosaurus skull was broad and flat with long jaws lined with needle-like teeth.
rejected.quote: The skull was broad and flat, with long jaws, lined with needle teeth
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'skull was broad and flat with long jaws'

rejected.statement: It is hypothesized that one branch of the nothosaurs may have evolved into pliosaurs such as Liopleurodon.
rejected.quote: It is thought that one branch of the nothosaurs may have evolved into pliosaurs such as Liopleurodon

rejected.statement: A 2014 phylogenetic analysis found both Lariosaurus and Nothosaurus to be polyphyletic, indicating a systematic revision of these genera is necessary.
rejected.quote: The analysis found both Lariosaurus and Nothosaurus to be polyphyletic in regard to each other and all the other genera of the family, making a systematic revision of these two genera necessary
